name: Maritime autonomy
thesis: Attritable autonomous surface and subsurface vessels, built at scale. Portfolio anchors: Saronic (Series D, 2026), Aeon. The question is not whether USVs work in a demo. It is which remaining problems gate fleets of thousands operating with one human per many hulls, in contested, GNSS-denied water.

nodes.label: One operator, many hulls
nodes.why: The economic unlock for attritable fleets. Today supervision ratios are closer to 1:1. Every node below is a gate on this one.

nodes.label: Radar + EO/IR fusion in sea clutter
nodes.why: Small boats and floating objects hide in wave clutter. Fusion that holds in sea state 4+ is the difference between a demo and a deployment.

nodes.label: Small-object detection on water
nodes.why: Mines, swimmers, small craft, debris. Benchmarks exist (SeaDronesSee, MaSTr) but real-time detection at range in glare and chop is still research.

nodes.label: Low-light and thermal maritime perception
nodes.why: Most interesting operations happen at night. Thermal datasets at sea are thin, so this is a data bottleneck more than a model one.

nodes.label: Visual odometry on open water
nodes.why: Water has no stable features. VO and SLAM that work on roads fail here. Whoever solves it removes the GPS dependency for the cheapest sensor on the boat.

nodes.label: Coastline and bathymetry-relative localization
nodes.why: Match what the sensors see to charts and terrain. Mature for UUVs with sonar, immature for cheap USVs with cameras and radar.

nodes.label: Multi-vessel cooperative localization
nodes.why: A fleet can localize itself by sharing relative measurements. Distributed filters are the active research front and they scale with fleet size.

nodes.label: GNSS-denied navigation
nodes.why: Jamming and spoofing are the default in contested water. No cheap, reliable, multi-day solution exists for small hulls. This is the single most valuable blocked node in the sector.

nodes.label: Intent prediction for manned vessels
nodes.why: You cannot follow the rules of the road without guessing what the other boat will do. AIS-trained trajectory models are good; behavior under non-cooperative actors is not.

nodes.label: COLREGs-compliant planning at sea
nodes.why: The rules of the road are written for humans. Encoding them so a planner is both compliant and provably safe is the gating problem for operating near manned traffic.

nodes.label: Learned control policies that transfer to real water
nodes.why: RL policies trained in sim are strong in sim. Transfer across sea states and hull dynamics is where they break.

nodes.label: Swarm task allocation and formation
nodes.why: Well studied in theory and in sim for a decade. Mostly solved when comms are good. The hard version is the next node.

nodes.label: Coordination without comms
nodes.why: Jammed fleets must still act together. Requires shared intent models and predictable behavior under silence. Very few groups work on the maritime version.

nodes.label: Surface and subsurface teaming
nodes.why: A USV acting as comms relay and launch platform for UUVs multiplies reach. Acoustic links and docking are the gates.

nodes.label: Resilient over-the-horizon comms
nodes.why: Mesh, LEO SATCOM, and acoustic links each fail differently. The fleet needs all three and a planner that knows which one is up.

nodes.label: High-fidelity marine simulation
nodes.why: You cannot run a million sea trials. Sims like HoloOcean and procedurally generated coastlines are the training ground. Fidelity of waves and sensors is the gap.

nodes.label: Fast hydrodynamic system identification
nodes.why: Every new hull needs a dynamics model before autonomy works. Data-driven and physics-informed methods cut that from months to days, which is what mass production needs.

nodes.label: Wave and weather disturbance modeling
nodes.why: Control and perception both degrade with sea state. Short-horizon wave prediction on board is the unlock for both.
queries: ship motion forecasting deep learning waves

nodes.label: Multi-week endurance power
nodes.why: Persistent presence is the mission. Wave, solar, and hybrid power systems exist at small scale; reliability over months is the gate.

nodes.label: Hull production at automotive rates
nodes.why: Boats are built like boats. Thousands of attritable hulls per year needs composite or additive processes that do not exist in the industry yet.

nodes.label: Modular payload integration
nodes.why: Same hull, many missions. Open standards for power, data, and mounting let a fleet change role in hours.

nodes.label: Assurance of learned maritime autonomy
nodes.why: Navies and insurers need proof, not demos. Runtime monitors and formal verification of learned controllers at sea are early. Whoever owns this owns certification.

nodes.label: Detect and defeat hostile USVs
nodes.why: Black Sea operations proved cheap USVs sink ships. The counter is now a market of its own and the research is a year old.

nodes.label: Autonomous mine countermeasures
nodes.why: The first mission navies hand to robots because it is the one humans least want. Sonar ATR is good, the full autonomous detect-to-neutralize loop is not.

nodes.label: Fleet-scale maritime domain awareness
nodes.why: Thousands of cheap sensors on the water beat one expensive one. Fusing them into one picture is a data problem that no vessel company has solved.
